overview: DexCom designs, develops, and commercializes continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) systems used by people with diabetes and, increasingly, metabolic health consumers to track glucose levels in real time. Its current flagship product is the Dexcom G7 platform (including the longer-wear G7 15 Day sensor), supplemented by Stelo, the first FDA-cleared over-the-counter glucose biosensor for adults with prediabetes and non-insulin-using Type 2 diabetes. The company sells primarily in the U.S. with a growing international business, and its razor/razorblade model (durable transmitter/app plus recurring disposable sensors) generates highly recurring revenue from a large and growing installed base of users.

business_model.summary: DexCom operates a razor/razorblade model: it sells a reusable transmitter/reader hardware component at low or subsidized margin and derives the large majority of revenue from recurring, high-margin disposable sensors that patients must replace every 10-15 days. This creates highly recurring, subscription-like revenue tied to the size of the active patient base rather than one-time hardware sales. Revenue is split between direct-to-consumer/durable medical equipment channels (largely U.S., reimbursed by insurance/Medicare) and distributor sales internationally. The August 2024 launch of Stelo opened a new, largely cash-pay/OTC consumer revenue stream targeting the much larger population of non-insulin-using Type 2 and prediabetic consumers, and the 2026 Nutrisense acquisition extends the model toward subscription-based nutrition/coaching services layered on top of the sensor.
business_model.customer_type: B2C-driven demand (patients/consumers) fulfilled through B2B channels: durable medical equipment (DME) distributors, pharmacy channel, and direct payor/PBM relationships; also licenses CGM data streams to insulin pump and digital health partners (Tandem, Insulet, Medtronic-adjacent ecosystems)
business_model.geographic_mix: United States approximately 70% of revenue, International (Europe, Japan, Canada, and expanding emerging markets) approximately 30% and growing faster than the U.S. (Q2 2026: U.S. +11% YoY, International +19% YoY)

main_competitors: Emerging low-cost entrants (Sinocare, POCTech, and other Asia-based CGM makers)
competitive_position.market_position: One of the two dominant global CGM players alongside Abbott. DexCom holds an estimated 60%+ share of the U.S. Type 1 diabetes CGM segment and roughly 70-74% of the broader U.S. CGM market, but only about 34% of global CGM shipments versus Abbott's ~53-58%, reflecting Abbott's much larger and faster-growing international/non-insulin footprint via FreeStyle Libre.

moat_factors.description: Physicians and patients build workflows, insulin-dosing algorithms, and pump integrations around a specific CGM; switching disrupts therapy management and often requires payor re-authorization

iCGM accuracy standards and years of clinical trial data (e.g., pediatric, pregnancy, hospital-use indications) create high barriers for new entrants; DexCom has among the longest track record of FDA-cleared indications

Non-exclusive integration agreements with Tandem, Insulet, and automated insulin delivery systems make DexCom sensors a default choice within multiple pump ecosystems, though the same interoperability also lets rivals plug into those ecosystems
Strong reputation for accuracy in Type 1/intensive insulin use, though Abbott has closed much of this perception gap with FreeStyle Libre 3

Recently secured coverage across all four largest commercial PBMs for all people with diabetes, widening addressable market, but reimbursement is a shifting political/payor landscape rather than a durable structural advantage

weaknesses: Structurally lower global market share and weaker non-insulin/Type 2 penetration than Abbott, which dominates the larger and faster-growing OTC/basal-insulin segment internationally
Product-cycle execution risk: a 2024 guidance miss (~40% single-day stock decline) exposed vulnerability to sales-force and channel-mix missteps
Heavy reliance on U.S. reimbursement and DME channel economics, which are being reshaped by CMS competitive bidding starting in 2027-2028
Narrower product portfolio than Abbott or Medtronic, which sell broader diabetes/metabolic device and pump lines that can cross-subsidize CGM competition
History of gross margin volatility from freight, scrap, and manufacturing ramp costs during product transitions (G6 to G7, G7 to G7 15 Day)

growth_drivers: G7 15 Day sensor rollout and conversion of the existing U.S. base (targeting near 50% conversion by year-end 2026), extending wear time and improving unit economics/gross margin
Stelo and the broader non-insulin Type 2/prediabetes and metabolic-health opportunity, a market many times larger than the intensive-insulin population DexCom has historically served
Expanded payor coverage - all four largest U.S. commercial PBMs now cover CGM for all people with diabetes, opening access to over 7 million additional non-insulin Type 2 patients
International expansion, including new market launches and the Flex sensor platform outside the U.S., where DexCom's share is much lower than Abbott's and has more runway

Product/software platform extension beyond glucose sensing toward a broader "biosensing"/metabolic health company, including the pending Nutrisense acquisition (nutrition coaching, registered dietitian access) layered onto the CGM data stream
Next-generation G8 sensor system in development, aimed at further miniaturization, accuracy, and cost-of-goods reduction
Continued deepening of insulin pump/AID interoperability partnerships (Tandem, Insulet) sustaining CGM attachment as the default sensor in automated insulin delivery
New $1 billion share buyback program (replacing a largely exhausted prior authorization) signaling capital return alongside growth investment

business.risk: Intensifying competition from Abbott FreeStyle Libre
business.description: Abbott's larger global share, lower price points, and broader non-insulin penetration pressure DexCom's growth and pricing, especially outside the U.S. and in Type 2/OTC segments
The July 2024 guidance miss and subsequent management turnover show the business is sensitive to sales-force restructuring, channel mix shifts (DME vs. pharmacy), and demand forecasting errors
Simultaneous global rollout of G7 15 Day and future G8 sensors carries manufacturing ramp, inventory, and customer-conversion execution risk

business.risk: Customer concentration in a narrow core indication historically
business.description: Historical revenue concentration in intensive insulin users limits total addressable market versus broader OTC ambitions now being pursued

financial.description: Freight, scrap, and manufacturing-ramp costs during product transitions have periodically compressed margins even as long-term trend is improving (guided ~64% non-GAAP gross margin for FY2026)
Roughly 30% international revenue exposes results to euro, yen, and other FX moves; a strong dollar can create translation headwinds
The pending Nutrisense acquisition and expansion into adjacent services introduce integration and capital-allocation execution risk

regulatory.description: CMS extended competitive bidding to CGMs/receivers in late 2025, with contracting starting 2027 and payment changes in 2028, threatening reimbursement rates and channel economics
Broad-based, durable third-party coverage is not guaranteed; administrative and contractual reimbursement challenges are recurring and could tighten under budget-constrained payors
As Stelo and similar OTC biosensors reach a much larger population outside clinical diabetes care, marketing claims and direct-to-consumer advertising face increasing regulatory and legal attention

macro.risk: Healthcare cost/reimbursement tightening in a high-rate or fiscally constrained environment
macro.description: Government and commercial payors under budget pressure could slow coverage expansion or reduce reimbursed prices

macro.risk: Tariff/trade policy on medical device components
macro.description: Global electronics and device supply chains (including new Ireland manufacturing capacity) carry exposure to tariff and trade-policy shifts, though DexCom's manufacturing footprint diversification partially mitigates this

macro.risk: Consumer discretionary spending on OTC/cash-pay products
macro.description: Stelo and similar non-reimbursed products are more exposed to consumer spending cycles than insurance-reimbursed CGM

macro_factors.industry_outlook: The global CGM market is forecast to keep growing at a double-digit CAGR through the 2030s, driven by rising diabetes/prediabetes prevalence, expanding reimbursement for non-insulin Type 2 patients, and the shift from fingerstick testing to continuous, connected sensing; a large majority of the world's diabetic population remains untapped, particularly outside intensive insulin therapy.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low to moderate - core CGM demand for insulin-dependent patients is largely non-discretionary and reimbursement-driven, but the newer OTC/cash-pay (Stelo) and international commercial segments carry more macro/consumer sensitivity
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (no meaningful debt-service burden disclosed as a key risk), moderate indirect sensitivity via growth-stock valuation multiple compression in a higher-rate environment
key_input_costs: Manufacturing labor and scrap/yield costs during product transitions

recent_developments.event: DexCom trading near 52-week highs following strong Q2 2026 results and raised full-year guidance; consensus analyst rating remains Moderate/Strong Buy with average price targets in the high-$80s to $90 range

Q2 2026 revenue of $1.308 billion, up 13% YoY (U.S. +11%, International +19%); non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 64.1% from 60.1%; net income up 46% YoY to $269.1 million; full-year 2026 revenue guidance raised to $5.18-$5.25 billion (~11-13% growth) with non-GAAP gross margin ~64% and operating margin ~23.5-24%
DexCom secured CGM coverage across all four largest U.S. commercial PBMs for all people with diabetes, opening access to more than 7 million additional non-insulin Type 2 diabetes patients
Agreement to acquire Nutrisense, a nutrition/coaching platform, to extend the CGM data stream into personalized dietitian-guided behavior-change services

Activist investor Elliott Investment Management disclosed a significant stake and reached a cooperation agreement with DexCom; company agreed to add two independent directors with MedTech/operations experience, renamed its board technology committee to the Operations and Innovation Committee, and authorized a new $1 billion share buyback program replacing a mostly-exhausted prior program

DexCom held its 2026 Investor Day, outlining an ambitious strategy to expand beyond core diabetes CGM into a broader biosensing/metabolic health company, alongside a preview of the next-generation G8 sensor and international Flex platform launch

CEO transition completed: Jake Leach (previously President/co-founder-era executive) assumed the CEO role from Kevin Sayer effective January 1, 2026; CFO Jereme Sylvain elevated to Chief Operating Officer, with Glenn S. Boehnlein added to the board as a new finance/MedTech-experienced director

Q3 2025 results and management commentary implying softer 2026 growth and margin pressure from elevated scrap and freight costs triggered a sharp double-digit after-hours stock decline, following a similar (~40% intraday) guidance-related selloff in July 2024 - underscoring recurring forecasting/execution risk that preceded the CEO change and Elliott involvement
Late-2025 CMS decision to extend the DMEPOS competitive bidding program to CGMs and receivers, with contracting to begin in 2027 and payment changes effective 2028

items.notes: Implies approximately 11-13% YoY growth; raised from prior full-year guidance following a strong Q2 beat
Driven by manufacturing efficiencies, improved freight costs, and growing mix of G7 15 Day sensors versus 10-day predecessor
Reflects operating leverage from revenue growth and gross margin expansion
Consistent with raised profitability guidance across the P&L
Key company-specific KPI tracking product-transition progress, a driver of both revenue mix and gross margin
Replaces prior authorization that had approximately $250 million remaining; announced alongside the Elliott Management cooperation agreement

guidance.management_commentary: New CEO Jake Leach and CFO/COO Jereme Sylvain have emphasized durable double-digit revenue growth, continued gross margin expansion through the G7 15 Day and future G8 transitions, and expanding the addressable market beyond intensive insulin users into Type 2 non-insulin and broader metabolic health/consumer biosensing via Stelo and the pending Nutrisense acquisition. Management has framed 2026 as an execution-focused year to rebuild credibility with investors after 2024-2025 guidance misses, while working constructively with activist investor Elliott Management on governance and capital allocation (including the new $1 billion buyback).

bull_case: Recurring, high-margin razor/razorblade sensor revenue model with a large and growing installed base supports durable double-digit revenue growth and expanding margins as G7 15 Day and G8 lower unit costs

Massive underpenetrated total addressable market in non-insulin Type 2 diabetes and prediabetes (tens of millions of U.S. patients), now unlocked by expanded PBM coverage and the Stelo OTC product plus Nutrisense's coaching layer

New CEO, elevated COO, added independent directors, and an activist investor (Elliott) aligned on governance and capital discipline provide a credible catalyst for improved execution and capital returns ($1B buyback) after a rocky 2024-2025
Structural moat in the core Type 1/intensive-insulin segment (60%+ U.S. share) via clinical data, physician trust, and deep interoperability with Tandem and Insulet pump ecosystems
Secular tailwind from rising global diabetes/prediabetes prevalence and a broader industry shift from fingerstick testing to continuous, connected, data-driven glucose and metabolic monitoring
bear_case: Abbott's FreeStyle Libre is larger globally (roughly 53-58% share vs. DexCom's ~34%), cheaper, and faster-growing in the higher-volume non-insulin/international segments DexCom is now targeting, meaning DexCom is chasing Abbott's stronghold rather than expanding from a position of strength

Track record of guidance misses and forecasting errors (July 2024's ~40% one-day drop; a further double-digit decline after Q3 2025 commentary) raises real execution risk that a CEO change alone may not resolve

CMS competitive bidding for CGMs, effective for contracting in 2027 and pricing in 2028, is a concrete, dated regulatory catalyst that could compress U.S. reimbursement economics, DexCom's most profitable channel

Margin guidance depends heavily on a smooth, well-forecasted transition to G7 15 Day and eventually G8; any repeat of past manufacturing/freight/scrap cost overruns would directly undercut the newly raised margin targets

Activist involvement (Elliott) and a strategic pivot toward becoming a broader "biosensing" company (Nutrisense, metabolic health) introduce integration, capital-allocation, and strategic-focus risk at a time when the core competitive fight with Abbott still needs to be won
